drafted_from: tool:remove-objects-from-an-s3-store row in tool-rows.json, do-work/remove-objects.ts and test/remove-objects.test.ts
start_here: Say to your AI: "Remove these three files from my files store: site/old/a.html, site/old/b.png, site/old/c.css." It runs tool:remove-objects-from-an-s3-store with that exact list and answers, for each key, removed with its size, absent, or failed with why.
no_lists_because: It names no list: it removes objects by their exact keys from a bucket whose key the person keeps in their vault.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's five values in your vault under one name: <store>-key-id, <store>-secret, <store>-endpoint (an https root), <store>-bucket and <store>-region, each reaching only the store's host. The key never appears in a request.

2. Read first: your AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account with method tools:run, tool tool:remove-objects-from-an-s3-store and input {store, action: list, prefix}, and shows you the keys and sizes under that prefix.
3. Name the exact keys to remove; your AI runs the tool with {store, keys}. A prefix, a wildcard or a key named twice removes nothing.

4. Read the answer: each key removed (with its size), absent, or failed (with why). List the prefix again to see it empty. A refused key (401 or 403) means a current key for that store belongs in the vault.
